title: Cupcake Measurement Conversions: Cups to Grams
summaryShort: For cups to grams for baking, use 120 g per cup of all-purpose flour, 200 g of granulated sugar, 227 g of butter. 85 g of cocoa, 240 g of milk and 215 g of oil. Weigh ingredients on a scale for cupcakes that bake the same every time.
metaTitle: Cupcake Measurement Conversions: Cups to Grams
metaDescription: Use our cups to grams for baking chart for flour, sugar, butter, cocoa, milk and oil, plus oven temps and pan sizes. Bookmark it and bake with confidence.
sidebarBullets: Standard cupcake cup: fill about 2/3 full

sections.heading: Why Grams Beat Cups for Cupcakes
paragraphs: Grams beat cups because weight never changes, while a cup of flour can swing by 30 grams or more. That gap is enough to turn a soft cupcake into a dry one.
How you scoop matters. Dip and sweep a cup into the bag and you pack in extra flour. Spoon it lightly and you get less. A scale ignores all of that.
list: Cups change with packing, humidity and scoop style.
Grams give the same batter every bake.
One bowl on a scale means fewer dishes.
Recipes from other countries are almost always in grams.

sections.heading: Grams per Cup for Common Cupcake Ingredients
paragraphs: The table above lists the grams per cup for the ingredients I reach for most in cupcakes. I use the spoon and level method for flour and cocoa, and a firm pack for brown sugar.
Brands vary a little, so treat these as solid averages. If a recipe lists its own gram weight, always follow that number instead.
list: Flour and cocoa: spoon into the cup, then level with a knife.
Brown sugar: pack firmly until it holds its shape when tipped out.
Butter: one stick is 113 g, which is 1/2 cup
Milk and oil: weigh them too, since measuring cups hide small errors.

sections.heading: Why Flour Is the Biggest Risk
paragraphs: Flour is the ingredient where cups cause the most trouble, because it compacts so easily. Too much flour gives you tight, dry, crumbly cupcakes with a flat flavor.
Cake flour weighs less than all-purpose, about 110 g per cup. If you swap one for the other by volume, your batter will be off. Weigh both and the swap becomes simple.

sections.heading: Oven Temperature: Fahrenheit, Celsius and Gas Mark
paragraphs: Most cupcakes bake at 350°F, which is 175°C or gas mark 4. This is the middle setting that gives an even rise and a golden top.
Fan ovens run hotter, so drop the dial by about 20°C (25°F). Use an oven thermometer if your cupcakes brown too fast or sink in the middle.

sections.heading: Common Pan Sizes and How Much Batter They Take
paragraphs: A standard cupcake cup holds about 1/3 cup of batter when filled two thirds full. That gives you 12 cupcakes from roughly 2 to 2 1/2 cups of batter.
Smaller and larger cups need different amounts and bake times. Check them 3 to 4 minutes early for minis and a few minutes late for jumbo.
list: Mini cup (1 3/4 inch top): about 1 tablespoon of batter
Standard cup (2 3/4 inch top): about 1/3 cup of batter
Jumbo cup (3 1/2 inch top): about 1/2 cup of batter
8 inch square pan (20 cm): fits about 12 standard cupcakes' worth of batter.
9 x 13 inch pan (23 x 33 cm): fits about 24 cupcakes' worth of batter.

sections.heading: How to Switch to Weighing in Your Kitchen
paragraphs: The easiest switch is to put the bowl on the scale and press the tare button after each ingredient. You skip the measuring cups and add everything in one bowl.
Start with a scale that reads in 1 gram steps. Write the gram weights on your favorite recipe cards so you only convert once.

howToSteps: Set a digital scale to grams and place your mixing bowl on it.
Press tare to reset the scale to zero.
Add flour first, using the grams per cup from the table above.
Press tare again before each new ingredient.
Weigh liquids like milk and oil in grams, not cups.
Check the oven dial against the Fahrenheit, Celsius and gas mark list.
Fill each cupcake cup about two thirds full, based on your pan size.

faq.question: How many grams are in a cup of all-purpose flour for cupcakes?
faq.answer: One cup of all-purpose flour is about 120 grams when spooned and leveled. If you scoop straight from the bag, it can weigh 140 grams or more.

faq.question: Is a cup of milk the same weight as a cup of oil?
faq.answer: No. A cup of milk is about 240 grams, while a cup of oil is about 215 grams. Oil is lighter, so never swap the gram weights.

faq.question: What is 350°F in Celsius and gas mark?
faq.answer: 350°F is 175°C (some ovens use 180°C) and gas mark 4. It is the standard temperature for most cupcakes.

faq.question: How many grams is one stick of butter?
faq.answer: One US stick of butter is 113 grams, or 1/2 cup. Two sticks make 1 cup, which is 227 grams.

faq.question: Do I need to adjust the oven for a fan setting?
faq.answer: Yes. Lower the temperature by about 20°C (25°F) on a fan oven. Fan heat browns the tops faster than a regular oven.
